Question: A triangle with vertices \(A(0, 2),\) \(B(-3, 2),\) and \(C(-3, 0)\) is reflected about the \(x\)-axis, then the image \(\triangle A'B'C'\) is rotated counterclockwise about the origin by \(90^{\circ}\) to produce \(\triangle A''B''C''.\) Which of the following transformations will return \(\triangle A''B''C''\) to \(\triangle ABC?\)

Choices.A:
counterclockwise rotation about the origin by
\(90^{\circ}\)
Choices.B: clockwise rotation about the origin by \(90^{\circ}\)

Solution:
Follow a general point \((x,y)\) through the two transformations. Reflection across the \(x\)-axis keeps the horizontal coordinate and reverses the vertical coordinate:
\[
(x,y)\longmapsto(x,-y).
\]
A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation sends \((u,v)\) to \((-v,u)\): rightward displacement becomes upward, and upward displacement becomes leftward. Applying this rule to \((x,-y)\) gives
\[
(x,-y)\longmapsto(y,x).
\]
Thus the combined transformation swaps the coordinates. Reflection across \(y=x\) also swaps the coordinates, because folding across this diagonal exchanges the horizontal and vertical directions. It therefore sends \((y,x)\) back to \((x,y)\).

This restores every vertex, so the required transformation is reflection about \(y=x\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
